$comment: Coverage matrix for the corpus, KEYED BY SLUG. A corpus file is `NN-slug` or `NN-slug-VARIANT`; the leading number is the spec's ordering, not an identity, and keying on it meant every upstream renumbering invalidated the whole matrix at once - 126 entries, none of which had changed. `covered` names the representative example by its slug too, and the scripts resolve it back to a numbered file. Matches carve-js#528, carve-rs#438 and carve-php#628. One golden records a KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE rather than blessing it: in `a-marker-separator-is-a-space-never-a-tab` the `:  d` line is scoped as a definition description, where the engines render the whole document as one paragraph - the term line above it was disqualified by its tab, and a line-oriented grammar cannot see that. Line one, which carries the rule, IS pinned. Tracked in markup-carve/carve-grammars#91.

skip.a-backslash-in-a-link-destination-is-a-l: How a backslash inside a destination is interpreted is link parsing; the link tokens are covered by 03 and the escape token by 60.
skip.a-bare-attribute-block-on-its-own-line-i: Negative case: '{}' stays literal. The attribute-block pattern requires at least one character, so there is no token to assert; block attribute lines are covered by 84.
skip.a-continuation-row-needs-a-body-row: Negative/structural case for table continuation rows; the '+' continuation marker token is covered by the table-continuation pattern exercised in 40/09.
skip.a-floating-attribute-stops-at-the-item-b: Where a pending attribute stops attaching is block semantics, not a token: the `{.c}` line carries the same attribute-block scopes wherever its scope ends, so there is nothing distinct to assert.
skip.a-pipe-pair-with-no-cell-is-not-a-table: Negative case: '||' must not become a table. TextMate matches on the line shape alone and has no positive scope to assert here; table tokens are covered by 09.
skip.abbreviation-definition-interrupts-a-par: Whether an abbreviation definition interrupts a paragraph is block-structure parsing; the definition token is covered by 14.
skip.abbreviation-definition-separator-must-b: Separator strictness is parsing: a definition either matches or stays prose. The matching case is pinned by `abbreviations`, and the non-matching case has no token by definition.
skip.abbreviation-matches-on-word-boundaries-: Abbreviation usage in prose is not highlighted at all (only the definition is, covered by 14); word-boundary matching is a resolver concern with no token.
skip.abbreviation-title-escapes-its-markup-ch: Escaping inside the title changes the rendered text, not the scopes - the title is one unquoted string token either way, pinned by `abbreviations`.
skip.adjacent-slash-and-underscore-emphasis-n: Nesting order between two emphasis kinds; both scopes are pinned by `emphasis`, and TextMate has no token for which one won.
skip.all-space-verbatim-content: Whitespace-only verbatim content is still one raw-inline run - same three tokens as `inline-code`.
skip.an-invisible-line-does-not-cancel-a-blan: Looseness is a rendering decision with no token of its own - the comment and the paragraph carry the same scopes whether the item comes out tight or loose. The comment token itself is covered by a-comment-is-recognized-at-any-column.
skip.attribute-block-after-a-mention-stays-li: Whether the braces bind to the mention is parsing; both the mention tokens and the attribute tokens are pinned (`mentions-and-tags`, `attributes`).
skip.attribute-braces-on-a-list-item-marker-l: Attributes on a marker line produce the marker tokens and the attribute tokens, both already pinned by `lists` and `attributes`.
skip.attribute-edge-cases: Attribute parsing edge cases; the attribute tokens themselves are covered by 17 and 75-style cases, with no new scope per edge.
skip.attribute-order-on-an-unwrapped-heading: Which attribute lands on which element is a render-time question; the tokens are pinned by `attributes` and `headings`.
skip.autolink-display-keeps-the-raw-content: Keeping the raw autolink content in the display text is a render concern; the autolink tokens (scheme and email forms) are covered by 59-autolinks.
skip.bare-dot-ordered-markers: The bare `.` is an ordered marker and scopes as one - the same `markup.list.numbered` token `ordered-list-start-and-delimiter` pins. Which value it starts at is not a highlighting distinction.
skip.bare-urls-stay-literal: Bare URLs are intentionally left as plain text with no scope; the point of the category is the absence of a link token.
skip.below-content-column-div-body-in-a-list-: Whether the body is inside the div depends on the content column, which needs block context; the div and list tokens are pinned by `fence-opener-with-a-nested-list-body-inside-a-list-item`.
skip.blocked-span-marker-renders-as-empty-cel: How a blocked span marker resolves to an empty cell is table-layout resolution; the '^'/'<' marker tokens are covered by 10-tables-with-rowspan-and-colspan and 96.
skip.blockquote-caption-after-a-blank-line: Caption association across a blank line is a block-structure/parse concern; the caption and quote tokens themselves are covered by 07 and 09.
skip.blockquote-lazy-continuation: Lazy continuation is block-structure parsing; the blockquote token is covered by 07.
skip.blockquote-lazy-continuation-stops-at-a-: Lazy-continuation termination at a fence is block-structure parsing; quote and fence tokens are covered by 07 and 11.
skip.blocks-that-render-to-nothing: Rendering to nothing is a render-time outcome; the blocks still scope, and those scopes are pinned by `comments` and `definition-lists`.
skip.bold-italic-delimiter-needs-content: Negative case: an empty `/*..*/` run stays literal. The absence of a scope is the point, and the positive form is pinned by `emphasis`.
skip.classes-are-deduplicated: Class deduplication happens when emitting the class attribute; both duplicates tokenize identically as class names, which are covered by 17-attributes.
skip.collapsed-reference-link: A collapsed reference link tokenizes the same as a reference link (covered by 34); collapsing is a resolver concern.
skip.colon-fence-as-a-block-opener-in-a-list-: The opener produces the same div tokens wherever it sits, pinned by `fence-opener-with-a-nested-list-body-inside-a-list-item`.
skip.colspan-marker-scans-left-past-a-consume: Left-scanning of a colspan marker across consumed cells is table-layout resolution; the marker tokens are covered by 10 and 96.
skip.comment-fence-with-trailing-text: The trailing text after the fence is inside the comment either way - one `comment.block` token, pinned by `comments`.
skip.compact-list-blocks: List compactness/looseness is block structure with no distinct token; bullets covered by 05.
skip.cross-references-resolve-inside-footnote: Cross-reference resolution scope is a resolver concern; the crossref and footnote tokens are covered by 58 and 43.
skip.cyclic-cross-reference-resolves-to-one-l: Cycle-breaking during cross-reference resolution is a render-time concern; the crossref token is covered by 58.
skip.definition-list-as-a-first-class-block-o: Opening a list without a preceding paragraph is block structure; the term and definition tokens are pinned by `definition-lists`.
skip.doubled-emphasis-delimiters: Doubled-delimiter handling resolves to the same emphasis/strong tokens covered by 01-emphasis.
skip.emphasis-edge-cases: Emphasis edge cases (delimiter runs, flanking) are covered representatively by 01-emphasis, 71, and 74; per-edge structural variants add no new scope.
skip.emphasis-opener-slash-adjacency: Flanking rules decide whether a delimiter opens; the resulting tokens are the ones `emphasis` already pins.
skip.emphasis-span-closes-before-a-following-: Which delimiter closes a run is parsing; the span tokens are pinned by `emphasis`.
skip.empty-delimiters: Empty delimiter runs deliberately produce no emphasis token; there is no positive scope to assert.
skip.escape-coverage: Exhaustive escape coverage is a parser concern; the escape token is covered by 60-escapes.
skip.fence-folds-as-lazy-inline-code-above-th: Whether a fence opens a block or folds into a paragraph as inline code is block context, which a line-based grammar does not have; the list tokens are pinned by `lists`.
skip.footnote-definition-inside-a-container-i: Collecting a footnote definition out of a blockquote or list is a resolver concern; the quote/list and footnote-definition tokens are covered by 07, 05 and 43.
skip.footnote-definition-requires-an-inline-b: A body-less definition stays prose; the well-formed case is pinned by `footnotes`.
skip.footnote-definition-separator-must-be-a-: Separator strictness is parsing; the definition tokens are pinned by `footnotes`.
skip.footnote-with-multiple-blocks: Multi-block footnote bodies are block structure; the footnote reference/definition tokens are covered by 43.
skip.hard-line-breaks: A trailing backslash hard break is not given a distinct scope by the grammar; it is a render-time line-break concern.
skip.headerless-table-alignment: Same cell/separator tokens as a normal table; headerless-ness is structural, not a scope difference.
skip.headings-inside-containers-are-not-wrapp: Section wrapping is a render-time structure; inside a container the heading produces the tokens `headings` already pins.
skip.image-trailing-attribute-is-strict-about: Glue strictness decides whether the braces bind; both the image and the attribute tokens are already pinned.
skip.implicit-heading-references-with-no-defi: Whether a reference resolves to a heading is a later pass; the heading and reference tokens are pinned by `headings` and `reference-link`.
skip.indented-attribute-line-stays-literal: Negative case: an indented attribute line is prose. A line-based grammar cannot tell that from a valid attribute line inside a list item (see markup-carve/carve-grammars#71), so it scopes as `attributes` here deliberately.
skip.indented-colon-fence-blocks-stay-literal: Negative case: an indented `:::` opens nothing. The line-based grammar scopes it as `admonitions` deliberately (markup-carve/carve-grammars#71).
skip.indented-image-and-caption-stay-literal: Negative case for indented blocks; the image and caption tokens are pinned by `image-with-caption`.
skip.indented-ordered-marker-content-column-i: A content-column rule with no token of its own; the marker and table tokens are pinned by `ordered-list-start-and-delimiter` and `tables`.
skip.indented-reference-and-footnote-definiti: Negative case: indented definitions are prose. Same line-based limitation as the other indented categories; the definition tokens are pinned by `reference-link`.
skip.leading-attribute-brace-before-an-inline: Negative case for brace binding; the attribute and critic tokens are pinned by `attributes` and `editorial-markup-takes-a-trailing-attribute`.
skip.line-blocks: A line block (::: | ... :::) tokenizes via the div opener/closer already covered by 44-generic-divs; line-block semantics are render-time.
skip.link-destination-parentheses-balance: Where a destination ends is link parsing, not highlighting; the link tokens are pinned by `links`. Renamed upstream from link-destination-stops-at-the-first-parenthesis - the rule changed from "stops at the first parenthesis" to balanced nesting, and neither spelling adds a token.
skip.link-reference-definition-separator-must: Separator strictness is parsing; the definition tokens are pinned by `reference-link`.
skip.list-lazy-continuation: List lazy continuation is block-structure parsing; list tokens are covered by 05.
skip.list-nesting-and-looseness: List looseness/nesting is block structure; bullet and ordered-marker tokens are covered by 05/52/53.
skip.literal-less-than-in-prose: A literal less-than in prose deliberately produces no autolink token; the point is the absence of a scope.
skip.mention-and-tag-name-boundaries: Name-boundary acceptance for mentions/tags is exercised by the mention/tag regex already covered by 15; the boundary edges are negative cases with no new positive scope.
skip.mention-ignores-email-addresses: Negative case: an email address must NOT become a mention. There is no positive scope to snapshot; the mention regex boundary is exercised by 15 and 89.
skip.nested-brackets-in-link-text: Nested brackets in link text is a link-parsing edge; the link tokens are covered by 03/34.
skip.nested-containers: Container nesting is block structure; the div/quote/list tokens are each covered by 44/07/05.
skip.nested-item-looseness-does-not-propagate: Looseness decides whether the renderer wraps item content in a paragraph; there is no token for it, and the list tokens are pinned by `lists`.
skip.non-breaking-space: A backslash-space non-breaking space is a render-time concern; the grammar does not scope it distinctly.
skip.only-the-id-hoists-to-the-section-wrappe: Hoisting is a render-time placement decision with no token of its own; `attributes` pins the id and class scopes.
skip.opaque-spans-inside-a-container: Opacity is about what the renderer descends into; the fence and div tokens are pinned by `fenced-code` and `admonitions`.
skip.openers-past-the-nesting-cap-are-one-par: The nesting cap is a parser depth limit; TextMate has no depth counter and scopes every `:::` opener the same way, so the degraded and undegraded documents tokenize identically.
skip.ordered-marker-vs-prose: Negative case distinguishing a real ordered marker from prose like '1985.'; marker tokens are covered by 52/53 and the prose case has no marker scope.
skip.outer-item-with-an-internal-blank-before: Same looseness question, from the blank-line side; no token either way.
skip.paragraph-interruption: Whether a construct interrupts a paragraph is block-structure parsing; the interrupting constructs are each covered by their own category.
skip.paragraph-trailing-whitespace: Trailing-whitespace stripping is a parser/render concern with no token-scope difference (plain paragraph text).
skip.parenthesized-ordered-marker: Carve does not treat parenthesized (1) as an ordered marker, so there is no marker token to snapshot (negative case).
skip.post-blank-list-continuation-content-col: The content column is block context; the marker tokens are pinned by `lists`.
skip.quote-flanking-after-an-escaped-characte: Flanking decides which smart quote is produced; the escape and quote tokens are pinned by `escapes`.
skip.reference-labels-are-case-sensitive: Case sensitivity of reference labels is a resolver concern; the reference tokens are covered by 34.
skip.scheme-probe-strips-unicode-whitespace: Unicode-whitespace stripping before the scheme probe is URL sanitization on output; the reference-definition token is covered by 34.
skip.security-hardening: Scheme and attribute sanitization (javascript:, ms-msdt:, onclick=, style=) happens on HTML output. A rejected URL or attribute tokenizes exactly like an accepted one, so there is no highlighting distinction; link/attribute tokens are covered by 03 and 17.
skip.single-line-headings: Carve heading markers are single-line and column-0, so a heading produces the same three tokens `headings` already pins. Renamed upstream from multi-line-headings when carve#451 made headings end at the newline; the category now asserts the opposite rule and still adds no token.
skip.smart-typography-escapes-and-code: Asserts that escapes and code spans suppress smart-typography; the escape and code tokens are covered by 60 and 12, and the suppressed sequences have no positive scope.
skip.strong-emphasis-starting-with-a-link: Interaction of strong emphasis with a leading link resolves to emphasis and link tokens covered by 01 and 03.
skip.sublist-marker-interrupts-a-continuation: Whether a marker opens a sublist or folds into the paragraph is block context; both marker kinds are pinned by `lists`.
skip.table-alignment-with-colspan: Colspan markers are covered by 10-tables-with-rowspan-and-colspan; the alignment interaction adds no new scope.
skip.table-as-a-block-opener-in-a-list-item: A table opens with the same row tokens wherever it sits, pinned by `tables`.
skip.table-cell-escaped-pipe: Whether an escaped pipe ends a cell is parser-level; the escape token itself is covered by 60-escapes and cell punctuation by 09-tables.
skip.table-cell-pipe-inside-code-span: A pipe inside an inline code span is a parse-boundary concern; code-span and table tokens are covered by 12 and 09.
skip.table-column-alignment: Column alignment is encoded in the separator-row colons; the grammar scopes the separator as a table header/separator token but does not distinguish per-column alignment, which is a render-time concern, not a highlighting distinction.
skip.table-doubled-alignment-marker: A doubled alignment marker is a parser edge case for layout; it produces no distinct highlighting token.
skip.table-multi-line-cell-continuation: Multi-line cell continuation is block structure; the continuation marker is covered by 100/83 and table cells by 09.
skip.table-per-cell-alignment-override: Per-cell alignment markers are not separately scoped from ordinary cell punctuation; alignment is a layout concern with no distinct token.
skip.table-row-closing-pipe: Whether the closing pipe is required is row parsing; the separator token is pinned by `tables`.
skip.table-rowspan-with-multi-line-content: Combines rowspan (covered by 10) with multi-line content (structural); no new distinct token.
skip.table-stacked-rowspan: Stacked rowspan is a layout/parse concern; the rowspan marker token is covered by 10.
skip.table-without-alignment: Produces the same cell/separator tokens as any table; the absence of alignment markers yields no distinct scope.
skip.tag-requires-a-word-boundary: Negative/boundary case for tag detection; no distinct positive scope beyond what 15-mentions-and-tags already covers.
skip.thematic-break-requires-contiguous-marke:
Negative case: a non-contiguous run is not a break. `* * *` and `_ _ _` stay unscoped, which is correct. The `-3` example is ` ***` with one leading space - NOT a break (the corpus renders it `

***

`) - and the ported rule DOES scope it, because `^\s*` cannot tell a top-level indent from a list item's content column, where a break is legitimate (`- item` then ` ---` renders `
`, measured against carve-js). Anchoring at column 0 instead would miss every break inside a list item or quote, which is the commoner shape. Same trade-off carve-grammars carries in the rule this ports, tracked in markup-carve/carve-grammars#94.
skip.tight-list-item-keeps-trailing-text-afte: Where trailing text attaches is block structure; the list and div tokens are pinned.
skip.trailing-attribute-block-edge-cases: Trailing attribute-block edges resolve to the attribute tokens covered by 17 and 84.
skip.trailing-whitespace-boundaries: Where the content of a verbatim run starts and ends. The literal-prefix tokens it also carries are pinned by `inline-literal`, and the plain run by `inline-code`.
skip.trojan-source-heading-ids-are-nfc-normal: NFC normalization and invisible-control stripping affect generated ids and output text, not tokens; the heading tokens are covered by 02 and 19.
skip.trojan-source-rendered-text-and-code-str: Bidi-override stripping is an output-sanitization concern; the surrounding text/code-span tokens are covered by 12-inline-code.
skip.two-char-delimiter-runs: Two-character delimiter runs resolve to the same emphasis tokens covered by 01-emphasis.
skip.unclaimed-openers-stay-literal: Negative case: a `:` that no symbol or extension claims stays prose. The claimed forms are pinned by `symbols`.
skip.under-indented-definition-attaches-over-: Attachment depends on the content column, which needs block context; the tokens are pinned by `definition-lists`.
skip.unresolved-footnote-reference-with-a-tra: Resolution happens after parsing and carries no scope; the reference and attribute tokens are pinned by `footnotes` and `attributes`.
skip.unresolved-reference-link: An unresolved reference link still tokenizes as a reference link; resolution status is not a highlighting distinction.
skip.unterminated-comment-fence: An unterminated fence runs to end of file, which is what the `comments` snapshot already shows; there is no separate scope for "never closed".
skip.widened-verbatim-fences: A wider fence changes the delimiter length, not the scope. The three run kinds it exercises are pinned by `inline-code`, `inline-literal` and `math`.
skip.wrapped-definition-term-continuation-bel: Whitespace stripping on a continuation line changes the text, not the scopes, which `definition-lists` pins.

skip.line-endings-and-a-byte-order-mark: measured, not assumed. Three of the four documents are outside a TextMate grammar's reach or already correct: an editor hands the tokenizer lines that are already split, so CRLF and a lone CR never reach a pattern, and the LF control scopes correctly. The fourth does not - a leading U+FEFF sits between the line start and the marker, and every block-opener pattern allows only spaces and tabs there, so a BOM-led file loses the scope on its first line (verified through shiki against this grammar: '# Title' colored #005CC5 without the mark, unscoped with it). Covering the category would pin one representative and measure neither fact. markup-carve/carve-grammars#154 carries the fix for the whole grammar family.
